title: My first mobile game money!!
author: HarvardHoodie
selftext: I am a software developer of 8+ years doing mostly web apps, SaaS, and contract work for web apps and SaaS. AI allowed me to get through the hurdles that stood in my way to making a game. Ive never been a huge art guy now I can get sufficient enough art to make a game. This is my first one its a farming themed idle game. I have many more coming but excited to get my first mobile app money. I feel like my CPM is really high no?

replies.author: Astro_Doughnaut
replies.body:
You can pay for play testers for that closed test. I used [https://www.testerscommunity.com/](https://www.testerscommunity.com/) \- just got approved for production a few days ago. They provide the answers you use in your production application (you mention that you paid for testers in the answers). They also gave me some great information the testers found about my app, which I used to fix/change some things. 

It's a 14 day closed test, lame but whatever.

replies.author: Flag_Shagger
replies.body: how much does it cost? I didn’t realise android needed playtesters…pretty insane since mobile app stores are loaded with junk

replies.author: Astro_Doughnaut
replies.body:
They have a $15 and a $25 option (plus more addons if you want). 

I went with the $25 option, they give you a detailed App Store Optimization report, and it's 25 testers instead of 15. I figured it was best to go for that to guarantee I reach the required numbers. Google will deny you if your testers don't actually test the app. 

I was surprised it had to be 12+ people for TWO WEEKS. Between that, waiting for my D.U.N.S number, and waiting for Steam to approve my stuff I'm just a sitting duck at this point.

replies.author: HarvardHoodie
replies.body:
Keep going!! Biggest piece of advice I can give not that mine is ultra successful. Focus on a MVP that is very light. Basic art focus on gameplay loop if you can make something you enjoy playing without good art and sounds you are on the right track. Focus on the details once you’ve made a fun initial gameplay loop. If you can’t find a fun gameplay loop move to the next idea.

I’m working on several games right now I’ve scrapped 2 or 3 they wernt as fun as I thought before spending a bunch of time making them look good and feel good. If your gameplay loop sucks no amount of art or other fun features will fix it.

Why I went with a simple well known loop for my first game didn’t reinvent anything added my own flavor to the genre.
